No AI tool has access to the company's data sets due to legal/PII concerns, bandwidth, and hallucination fears

Cross-referencing multiple dashboards/looks in Looker manually to derive insights

Dependency on other teams (data, finance) to get answers slows down decisions

The horrifying moment of seeing a Slack thread about something you were supposed to work on but didn't

Connect Claude to Slack to track project updates and surface upcoming dates in a centralized place
Build an AI-assisted project management office to integrate projects, due dates, and automate Slack reminders
Bolster the demand planning model (connecting data sets + merchandising plan) using AI

Team members at varying skill levels — Julia isn't using skills fully, R&D chef needs entry-level training

digest.name: Megan Gallagher
digest.currentWorkflow: Leads performance/paid media (Meta, Google, AppLovin) plus SEO and funnel/landing-page optimization; heavily uses Claude with custom skills and projects to review copy, automate reporting, and build assets, while working around the lack of MCP/API connections to internal data tools via scheduled Looker-to-Sheets exports.

painPoints.text: SEO/LLM-awareness work keeps getting pushed off because performance/paid media and high-CPA periods pull focus away
No good tool yet to track LLM awareness/citations and how the brand shows up in LLMs
Company doesn't use Shopify or Stripe, so enabling subscriptions/new members outside the website is a technical/legal hurdle
Heavy manual review of video ads and landing pages needed, and lost a resource when someone left the company
Very specific brand/health/FDA language requires slow, careful review of all copy before launch
Internal data (sales, channels, Mixpanel, GA4) is not connected to AI tools via MCP, forcing manual/scheduled exports as workarounds
Data team hasn't enabled AI agent connections to data tools, and there's fear of enabling it broadly due to accuracy/verification risk
Building GA4 dashboards is tedious — going in, building dashes across random periods to find answers
Manually building custom-box URL parameters from SKUs is tedious
Weekly WBR/report deck requires manual screenshotting and updating
Creative bottleneck: has to submit creative requests (e.g. banner copy swaps, image resizing) to the creative team, slowing lower-funnel testing
Too much noise on Slack, though she's organized it to a digestible level
Email automation (auto-forward via Google Studio) blocked by permissions
Can't turn a Google Doc task directly into an Asana task (only Google tasks), forcing manual workaround
Being fast/high-performing means work just piles back on instead of buying back time, contributing to overload/burnout risk
Ad hoc AI use — hasn't formalized skills or organized work into projects, so context isn't retained
Uncertainty about whether to use in-app AI (Slack, GA4) vs. Claude for cross-platform work

opportunities.text: Connect internal data (sales, Mixpanel, GA4, Looker) to Claude/Gemini via MCP for read/write, enabling conversational querying and reporting
Build a formalized skill to fully automate the weekly WBR report and deck insights
Set up anomaly detection and Slack/email alerts on conversion-rate and CPA changes broken down by channel
Use the brand-guidelines/FDA compliance skill across more copy use cases to speed review
Formalize a custom-box URL builder skill and share it company-wide
Adopt Notebook LM to isolate and synthesize campaign learnings (e.g. multiple scallop launches) without cross-contamination
Enable write-back MCP to ad platforms to auto-pause/replace ads when promos end
Stand up landing-page creation pipeline (Claude design → GitHub → Vercel) to remove creative bottleneck for lower-funnel testing
Use AI to forecast budget/spend allocation across channels based on prior-year CPA trends
Use Claude cowork on desktop to read/draft emails and manage Asana tasks cross-platform
Organize work into Claude projects to retain memory/context and stay organized
Have Megan lead lunch-and-learns to share her skills, gems, and integrations with colleagues

wants: A good tool to track LLM awareness/citations for the brand
All internal data flowing into Claude via MCP so she can just ask questions
To automate the weekly WBR report and deck
To automate turning off/replacing ads when promos end via MCP write-back
A landing-page hosting tool connecting Claude design → Vercel via GitHub with dev environments
To get better at automations and formalize her ad hoc skills
More succinct, bullet-point AI responses without excessive emojis
Time to explore and learn as part of her job
To enable people to subscribe/become members without visiting the site
needs: Data team to open up/enable MCP or AI-agent connections to internal data tools (Mixpanel, Looker, GA4)
Guardrails and verification practices for AI data accuracy before broad rollout
Permissions resolved for email/data automations
Training/guidance on Claude projects, skills formalization, and Claude Code/terminal + desktop cowork
A vetted landing-page tool and product/engineering support to build the Vercel/GitHub pipeline
Encouragement/permission to protect time gained back rather than immediately taking on more work
A forum (lunch-and-learns) to share and cross-pollinate her methods
digest.quote: I want all of our data — our internal data, spend, sales, channel by day by year — to be able to go into Claude, so I could just ask, like, hey, what's the difference year over year... I'm doing workarounds right now, but I think that would help everyone in the company.

digest.name: Clifford Borris
digest.currentWorkflow: Leads all creative, website development, brand identity and value-added content, working closely with the owner and a small team (ACD, senior designer, contractors). Increasingly acts as brand approver/stakeholder while trying to protect time for real creative work; already builds AI 'brand nugget' assets and custom GPTs to replace some functions.

painPoints.text: Waterfall production process where perspectives change midway, triggering a flurry of Slack/Asana communication and wasted, unused produced assets
Constant coordination overhead staying aligned with everyone whenever anything changes; ops person has to tap people and chase project management
Communication overload — 60,000 unread emails, ~200 Slack channels, paragraphs of Slack threads he mentally can't engage with
Over-communication and people's conjecture/opinions instead of just acting; upward delegation where capable people ask him to solve problems they should own
Ambiguity over decision ownership on cross-functional work — 'who's the decision maker?' constantly surfaces
Risk of missing important external vendor emails buried in the unread mountain
Always behind the curve; priorities get buried as work piles up
Owner is a busy micromanager who bottlenecks approvals on sensitive creative (ads with his face); work piles up waiting for sign-off
Monthly owner meeting requires tracking every project from memory; no consistent way to surface status, leading to last-minute scrambles
Increasing burden of being the brand-approval stakeholder — reviewing others' work all day when he'd rather create
No single source to track project milestones/checkpoints; has to dig through Asana or old Slack messages
New retail hard deadlines (e.g. packaging going to print) now create urgent pressure the flexible past workflow didn't
No agile learning loop — repeat campaigns (e.g. scallops) launched many times without capturing/reusing prior learnings; findings die in a Google Slides deck
Creative team sits at the end of the cycle without upstream data before creation
AI image generation for anything graphic (paid ads) fails — Claude Design outputs are HTML/CSS only and look bad
Landing page 'launch' side unsolved — page speed/optimization; Webflow lacks AI integration and engineering time takes forever
No workflow to flow assets between a library, Figma and Iterable (CRM) for email production
~$450k spent on product photo production, much of it basic/uninteresting; AI product-shot workflow still very manual (rough Photoshop comps fed through ChatGPT)
Big performance video agency (~$300k) produces garbage, gets messaging wrong, uses awful AI voiceover — bane of his existence
Maintaining brand info/skills across multiple platforms (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) — becoming an 'AI janitor' updating each when things change (e.g. wrong mission statement)
Tool sprawl / wild-west adoption — team tried Bolt, Replit, Lovable, etc.; now cutting credit card spend
Weak/ambiguous data policy — people unsure what 'sensitive data' actually means
High business variability (fish quotas, market prices) makes keeping a marketing calendar very hard
Team resistance framed as 'faster if I just do it myself' vs investing in AI workflows

opportunities.text: Email/Slack synthesis and triage — auto-summarize 200 Slack channels and surface important pending items and vendor emails so nothing is missed
A 'FYI' dashboard connected to Slack/Asana/email that proactively tracks changes, assigns accountability, and personalizes updates (FYI Cliff / FYI Emily)
Auto-compiled weekly project status view so he isn't scrambling before the monthly owner meeting
Notebook LM as a campaign-learnings hub (e.g. all scallop launches) to build an agile loop feeding data to creative before creation
Centralized brand source-of-truth (Obsidian-style vault / MD file) that cascades to all platforms so skills/GPTs/gems update from one place
Custom Gemini Gems leveraging the enterprise plan for copywriting and marketing assets, more flexible than Claude Design
Skill/flywheel connecting Notebook LM briefs into Claude to generate creative briefs and execute static ads tied to performance data
AI product photography workflow using their solo product shots as source data to replace much of $450k photo spend
In-house AI ad production to reduce reliance on the ~$300k performance video agency
Automate low-funnel/repeat marketing (product launches, email flows, recipe/newsletter content) so team can focus on brand-pillar Alaska storytelling
Agentic automation (make.com/n8n) to chain data-driven learnings into optimized, self-updating campaign execution
Lunch-and-learns to level up the eager team and standardize tools/practices

digest.currentWorkflow: Mary manages PR (agency + direct with Aaron Kallenberg), partnerships, and organic social, while collaborating with Cliff and Emily on creative development and product launches. Day to day she jumps across social, PR, and partnership verticals to understand what resonates, and uses Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini to fine-tune tone, draft copy, and analyze reporting.

painPoints.text: New social workflow routing everything through Aaron has slowed the team down, even though it added rigor to each post
Struggling to scale influencer and content creator programs
People constantly find and use the wrong/bizarre logos and keep asking for box photos and assets despite a centralized asset kit
Having to repeat where the asset kit lives 'a million times' like a broken record
Can't find things in Slack — lost Cliff's custom GPT link and other shared resources buried in Slack
Weirdly nuanced content categorization makes broad-stroke trend analysis hard
Data source gaps — Looker pulls from a manual weekly (not recent) Sprout report, so the company only sees a snapshot, not to-date performance
Constantly bouncing across reports and pulling in the data team to understand what's happening, especially at quarter end
Facebook group has very limited reporting capabilities and little external transparency
Building social dashboards is blocked by API limitations and mismatch between company data reporting and what the tools offer — 'banging our head against the wall' with the data team in Looker
Team is split between making content and reporting on insights, leaving too little time for insight development and sharing
Communication happens across too many places — Slack channels, DMs, and multiple Asana boards with varying levels of usage
Having to ping people 5 times in Slack to get reviews when they don't respond in Asana
Underuses Asana; feels her capabilities are the most basic and the experience isn't great
Overwhelmed by amount of inbound outreach (DMs + emails) with varying levels of detail, hard to evaluate and cherry-picking leaves opportunities on the table
AI-generated visuals/social images don't work well and 'come off as a joke,' limiting content creation use
AI clip generation from long-form video is 'not quite there'
Unclear guardrails on what business info can go into Claude vs Gemini — line between sensitive and non-sensitive data is fuzzy
Nervous to connect tools/integrations for fear of breaking rules or getting in trouble
Feeling generally overwhelmed by AI and unsure where to start
Has forgotten how to build Excel formulas manually

opportunities.text: Build a Claude skill that acts as a reporting analyst — ingest exported social/Excel reports in a set format, analyze for defined insights, and output a formatted report/deck
Define what a 'good insight' looks like for Claude so it surfaces non-obvious, usable insights that feed next posts and team comms
Connect Sprout Social / social data to Claude via connectors/MCP to interact with data directly and bypass Looker gaps
Create an automated social 'at-a-glance' dashboard showing platform health, notable tags/mentions, and inbound volume that can be shared in meetings
Automate inbound outreach triage — auto-request missing info and summarize weekly opportunities categorized as influencers, creators, and partnerships
Automate social/cultural/food trend monitoring and platform update tracking as a base layer for the team to riff off
Automate platform health monitoring to contextualize whether metric dips are company-specific or industry-wide
Turn brand guidelines into a Claude design system and use HTML swipe magazines for quick on-brand comms/decks
Create a Gemini gem / Claude skill as a recipe/copy writer trained on product and recipes for consistent tone
Build an Asana-expert gem/skill and connect Asana + Slack to Claude to automate review reminders and reduce manual pinging
Continue using AI voice cloner and social copy generation to speed script fixes (already saved ~2 weeks on a re-record)
Run focused lunch-and-learns with homework to build skills incrementally and reduce AI overwhelm

wants: Clear guidance on which AI platform to standardize on (Claude vs Gemini)
Clear guardrails on what business data can go into which tool
To automate daily/regular social reporting
A way to create better visibility into platform performance outside Looker
Automated trend and platform-health monitoring as a base layer
Automated triage/summary of inbound outreach with auto follow-up for missing info
To learn how to build skills and gems and fine-tune them
Focused, digestible lunch-and-learn training with homework
Notable social mentions/tags elevated so they don't get buried
needs: Explicit company policy on data sensitivity and which AI tool to use
Enterprise/team account access to enable Claude connectors safely
Hands-on training on building Claude skills and Gemini gems
Reassurance and clear rules so she isn't nervous about connecting integrations
Help defining insight criteria and output formats to configure AI effectively
Resolution of underlying data-source fragmentation (Looker/Sprout/manual reports)

digest.name: Emily Buckley
digest.currentWorkflow: Works exclusively in Claude (via Claude Desktop with some connectors set up) on a personal account, using a morning briefing that pulls from her calendar and email; oversees a team of ~27 people across marketing while trying to stay across many concurrent initiatives.

painPoints.text: Team knowledge is siloed — people learn and use AI individually without sharing how they use it, so skills and insights don't propagate across the team
Can't tell what's launching or happening when her director of marketing is out of town — lacks visibility into the many concurrent initiatives
Smart team members spend time on minutia like updating docs instead of higher-value thinking
No clear enterprise/team AI accounts — everyone on personal Claude accounts, creating uncertainty about data security and inability to share work
Unclear guidance on what counts as 'sensitive information' and what can safely be connected/uploaded (e.g. Looker, Asana)
People lack the time to learn and tinker with AI tools
High stakes discourage experimentation — people won't connect tools for fear of doing something wrong
Difficulty holding team accountable to OKR/roadmap dates; projects drag and she can't stay on top of 27 reports' deadlines
Bombarded with pings and doesn't know where projects stand or if they're on track
Fears being a bottleneck on reviewing/giving feedback on team initiatives at the right time
Her own Claude setup is incomplete — briefing doesn't auto-launch (needs manual click), hasn't connected Looker, still on personal account
Organization/CEO hasn't pushed LLMs from an enterprise perspective, so broader adoption stalls despite being an AI-friendly leader
Earlier Gemini rollout didn't stick — nobody adopted it
AI slop and 'AI talking to AI' appearing in Slack — low-effort AI output replacing human thinking

opportunities.text: Standardize the whole marketing team onto a single enterprise/team Claude account, rolled out as a moment at the off-site
Team-wide AI morning briefing so everyone knows what's launching each week (ops visibility)
Build a living Claude artifact/dashboard that surfaces project status (green/yellow/red), roadmap tracking, and flagged Slack items she missed
Automate minutia and repetitive workflows (doc updating) so team spends more time thinking
Use NotebookLM to consolidate past campaign assets and learnings (e.g. scallop launches) to surface trends and inform new campaigns
Establish shared/synchronized cross-team workflow with access to each other's work (creative, merchandising box-building, consumer insights)
Run short lunch-and-learns on specific topics (creating skills, connectors, artifacts) to spread capability
Clear published guidance on approved tools and what data is safe to use
Make marketing the model team to drive broader org adoption

wants: :Team buy-in and cohesive, non-siloed use of AI
AI helping with general operations and a team-wide briefing of what's launching
Automating minutia so smart people do more thinking
Enterprise/team Claude accounts with clear data-security answers
Everyone on the same Claude account, decided at the off-site
A living dashboard to track project/OKR status without being a bottleneck
A synchronized cross-team workflow where everyone can access each other's work
An aspirational ops layer with boards, OKRs, and timelines for big projects
No AI slop — humans still thinking, no AI-talking-to-AI
needs: Enterprise/team Claude accounts provisioned for the marketing team
Clear guardrails defining sensitive information and approved tools
Completed personal setup (auto-launching briefing, Looker connection, moving off personal account)
Structured lunch-and-learns on skills, connectors, and artifacts
Executive/CEO mandate to push enterprise LLM adoption
A norm/commitment against AI slop keeping humans in the loop
digest.quote: I don't want AI slop, I don't want AI talking to AI... I want the team to think. So that's the one big asterisk.

digest.currentWorkflow: Works as the connective tissue across every marketing vertical, leading quarterly planning and go-to-market, overseeing a team of four (integrated marketing manager, marketing PM, content ops managers, creative ops coordinator). painPoints.text: People struggle to stay looped in and on top of what they need to be working on; team keeps trying new announcements, calendars, and formats but hasn't 'struck gold' on getting people to pay attention
Fast-moving business with dramatically shifting inventory creates constant outliers that hit the plate and make it hard to get ahead despite robust processes
Automation for automation's sake in Asana that doesn't surface the right information, especially around timelines and workback schedules
Overview decks and quarterly planning decks require heavy manual upload and updating across Asana and the deck, with no single source of truth staying in sync
Cross-team finger-pointing and rework, e.g. merch team unhappy with assets on launch day requiring multiple conversations and a new process devised on the fly
She becomes everyone's 'personal Google' — the only highway of information because verticals work siloed and don't connect with each other
Constantly re-onboarding people to what's going on and chasing down people and information they thought was handled
Fragmented communication norms across email, Slack, and Asana — some people don't read Slack, some only read bolded/tagged items, some respond in email, causing lost information for a remote company

Team members are tunnel-visioned and siloed (Cliff 'like a goldfish' needing daily reminders, Jonathan tunnel-visioned on retention, Amy/Mary on new product), so they don't understand upstream/downstream implications of their decisions
Feels like a babysitter reminding people what to work on instead of having her team spend time on higher-value work
Manually mapping domino effects/timeline implications when a decision is made — what dates shift, what to communicate, risks and blockers — leaving room for human error
Manual financial tracking — actuals entered into Asana by hand for the whole marketing budget, work she says doesn't need to be manual and gets stuck inside Asana

analysis.companySummary: Wild Alaskan's marketing org is unusually eager and already experimenting with AI, but adoption is fragmented, individual, and stalled at the point where real data and shared workflows are needed. A handful of power users (Megan, Kelsey, Cliff) are building skills and connectors on personal accounts, while others (Jonathan, Mary, Emily) have ideas but no training, no sanctioned tools, and fear of touching sensitive data. The two biggest levers are organizational, not technical: standardize onto enterprise Claude accounts with clear data guardrails, and connect internal data (Looker, Mixpanel, GA4, Asana, Sprout) so people stop doing manual reporting and cross-referencing. Do those two things and a dozen high-impact quick wins — automated WBR decks, box configurators, campaign-learning hubs, priority briefs — unlock immediately.
tldr: Get the whole marketing team off personal AI accounts onto enterprise Claude with clear data rules — this unblocks everything else.
Manual reporting is the #1 time sink: automating the weekly WBR deck alone frees hours for Jonathan, Megan, Mary and Kelsey.
Your data is siloed and disconnected from AI; a read-only data-connection pilot is the highest-value bet.
Everyone asked for lunch-and-learns — Megan and Kelsey are ready-made champions to lead them.
People fear breaking rules; publish a one-page 'what data is safe' policy this week to release the brakes.
Guard against AI slop and compliance risk — keep humans reviewing all copy and member data stays out of prompts.
